# How to Draw Any Free-Body Diagram

<!-- STEP id="step-one" -->
## Step 1 — Isolate

Pick exactly one object.

Mentally lift it out of the scene. Everything touching it stays behind — only the object remains.

<!-- STEP id="step-two" -->
## Step 2 — List Every Force

- **Weight** — always present, pulling straight down.
- **Normal force** — only where it presses against a surface, pushing straight back.
- **Tension** — only where a string pulls it.
- **Friction** — only where it rubs against a surface.
- **Applied force** — any other direct push or pull.

<!-- STEP id="step-three" -->
## Step 3 — Draw Each Arrow

Start every arrow at the object.

Point it the way that force actually pushes or pulls. Label it.

<!-- STEP id="step-four" -->
## Step 4 — Apply Newton's Second Law

Add up the forces along each direction.

Not accelerating that way? They sum to zero. Accelerating? They sum to mass times acceleration.

**Isolate. List. Draw. Add up.**
